description: CGI.pm 4.55 query parsing in a minimal HTTP::Daemon balance handler, using the gateway's documented synthetic session and account values.
client: scripts/record.mjs: a raw TCP socket from the host to the published port; request targets are sent exactly as listed, with Connection: close.
substitutions: The service describes CGI.pm scripts behind Apache 1.3 since 1995. This records CGI.pm 4.55 from Debian 12 on the same pinned Perl base as the XML-RPC sets, not an installation of Apache 1.3 or a historical CGI.pm release.

HTTP::Daemon supplies the HTTP transport and passes the query string to CGI.pm's constructor unchanged. query.pl reads parameters in scalar context so CGI.pm selects the first repeated value. Only the gateway's documented balance and session-error reply logic is supplied by the recording handler; no query parser is reimplemented.

exchanges.name: encoded-token
exchanges.description: Percent-encoded plus, semicolon and equals remain literal token characters.

exchanges.name: literal-plus
exchanges.description: A literal plus decodes to space and changes the accepted token.

exchanges.name: literal-semicolon
exchanges.description: A literal semicolon splits parameters and truncates the token.

exchanges.name: semicolon-separators
exchanges.description: Semicolons separate the three parameters, before percent decoding their values.

exchanges.name: mixed-separators
exchanges.description: Ampersand and semicolon can both separate parameters in one query.

exchanges.name: first-value-valid
exchanges.description: The first repeated session value wins when it is valid.

exchanges.name: first-value-invalid
exchanges.description: A later valid session does not replace the first invalid value.

exchanges.name: name-only-session
exchanges.description: A parameter name without an equals sign has an empty value.

exchanges.name: empty-session
exchanges.description: An explicit empty value is not an accepted session.

exchanges.name: literal-equals
exchanges.description: Only the first equals sign separates a name and value; an equals inside the token remains data.

exchanges.name: lowercase-escapes
exchanges.description: Lowercase hexadecimal percent escapes decode to the same accepted token.
